Samir —

Quick technical answers and what we’ll need from your network team:

1) Control plane connectivity:
- For fully air-gapped installs we offer an on-prem control plane package (installer + offline updates). That setup removes the need for outbound control-plane traffic during steady state; only the admin workstation used for updates needs ephemeral outbound access for patch pulls.
- Semi-managed VPC: control plane components exist in a customer VPC with optional peering to Redwood management network for easier upgrades; we can also run a private-control-plane variant that only talks to your internal KMS.

2) HSM / KMS:
- We support KMIP-compatible HSMs (Thales, Utimaco) via our KMS integration layer. We’ll need to validate firmware version and KMIP profile. If you prefer cloud KMS, we support AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault as well.

3) Feature parity vs hyperscalers:
- Streaming: supported for both VPC and on-prem with the same API surface.
- Tool/function calls: supported, but for air-gapped installs we recommend a short stubbed adapter pattern for outbound tools to avoid external service calls; full tool integrations can be proxied through an internal service.
- Quantized performance: quantization profiles are supported on our runtime; raw throughput can differ vs hyperscalers depending on hardware and kernel selection. We’ll surface a per-test performance matrix during PoC.

4) Prompt constraints:
- No unusual tokenization differences compared to standard open LLMs. For p95 you’ll want to include representative conversation length and peak concurrent connections in the test window.

What we need from you to prepare:
- Network diagram (VPC subnets, firewalls, NAT rules)
- Host specs for on-prem nodes (CPU, GPU model, NIC speeds) if on-prem is an option
- KMS/HSM model and firmware details

I’ll attach a short technical checklist and the control plane decision matrix. Grace — looping you in to help schedule the test window and verify hardware assumptions.
